# Scope

> Scope is a free, open-source Linux app manager. It lists apps installed through APT, Snap, Flatpak, and AppImage in one searchable list, and it shows the exact commands for every update or uninstall before anything runs. Written in Rust with Zed's GPUI. Ubuntu is the first target. Version 0.3.4, MIT License.

Scope is a desktop app for Ubuntu and other Linux systems. It answers the question "what is installed on this machine, and how do I update or remove it safely?" It reads four package sources (APT, Snap, Flatpak, AppImage) plus desktop launchers that no package manager owns. Admin actions use the standard Polkit dialog, so the app never sees the user's password.

## Pages

- [Home](https://khurrambhutto.github.io/scope/): What Scope is, how a change works, supported sources, status, and FAQ.
- [Install](https://khurrambhutto.github.io/scope/install.html): Install the .deb on Ubuntu, build from source, verify updates, and remove Scope.
- [Safety](https://khurrambhutto.github.io/scope/safety.html): How previews, revalidation, APT simulation, the deny-list, and Trash protect the user.
- [Full text](https://khurrambhutto.github.io/scope/llms-full.txt): Everything above in one Markdown file, for AI tools that read a single document.

## Facts

- Name: Scope
- Category: Linux desktop package manager, app manager
- Platform: Linux, Ubuntu first, x86-64
- Sources: APT (manual installs), Snap (apps, runtimes hidden), Flatpak (user and system scopes), AppImage (listed only), desktop launchers (listed only)
- Actions: uninstall and update for APT, Snap, and Flatpak; AppImage update and uninstall are not supported yet
- Stack: Rust, Zed's GPUI, no webview
- License: MIT
- Author: Khurram Bhutto (https://khurrambhutto.tech/)
- Current release: v0.3.4 (https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope/releases/tag/v0.3.4)
